annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, full Algorithm 1.1 execution model, and exact Theorem 5.1 componentwise recurrence

assumptions: The dimension is positive and A is a nonsingular real square matrix, represented with a two-sided inverse action Ainv.
The stored iterates, computed residuals, and computed corrections form the unscaled Algorithm 1.1 refinement loop; x_0 is arbitrary because Theorem 5.1 imposes no initial-solve accuracy model.
The precisions satisfy uR <= u <= uS <= uF, uR is nonnegative, and gamma_p^r is valid for p equal to the maximum row nonzero count of [A b].
The residual computation and residual rounding satisfy the exact componentwise model (3.3).
The correction solver satisfies the exact componentwise defect model (2.5) for an iteration-dependent entrywise nonnegative G_i.
The rounded update satisfies the exact componentwise model (3.6).
Condition (5.6) holds for every iteration with cond(A^{-1}) represented as |||A||Ainv|||_infinity.
The run carries the M-matrix inverse M_i=(I-Z_i|Ainv|)^{-1}, its entrywise nonnegativity, and its infinity-norm bound by 2, exactly as derived from (5.6) immediately before Theorem 5.1.
The standard floating-point model excludes underflow and overflow, as stated in section 6.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p03_t3_componentwise_residual_recurrence {n : Nat} (run : P03ComponentwiseIRRun n) (i : Nat) : forall j : Fin n, |p03ComponentwiseExactResidual run (i+1) j| <= p03MatVec (p03W run i) (p03VecAbs (p03ComponentwiseExactResidual run i)) j + p03Y run i j
formal_statement.plain_language: Every computed Algorithm 1.1 iterate satisfies Theorem 5.1's exact componentwise residual recurrence with the paper's iteration-dependent Z_i, M_i, W_i, and y_i.

informal_proof: Derive (5.1) from the rounded update. Combine the residual model (3.3), solver model (2.5), and update model (3.6) to obtain (5.2) and the exact correction inequality c_i <= P_i*c_i + P_i*q_i, where c_i=Z_i|dHat_i| and P_i=Z_i|Ainv|. Apply the entrywise nonnegative inverse M_i to obtain c_i <= M_i*P_i*q_i, substitute this into (5.2), and distribute exactly to obtain W_i and y_i.
informal_statement: For every iteration of unscaled three-precision iterative refinement satisfying (2.5), (3.3), (3.6), and the uniform one-half condition (5.6), the next exact residual is bounded componentwise by W_i times the previous exact residual magnitude plus y_i, with the exact formulas printed in Theorem 5.1.

tier_rationale: The L proof can reuse NumStability.abs_matMulVec_le, and the frozen library also contains generic componentwise resolvent and iterative-refinement ingredients. It does not contain the three-precision Algorithm 1.1 execution model, the iteration-dependent Z_i/M_i construction, or the exact W_i/y_i theorem. Completing the task still requires deriving the paper-specific correction inequality and assembling the noncommutative componentwise recurrence, so the selected result remains an extension task.
